title: Arini’s Head of US Investments Gavin Yates Leaves Hedge Fund
summary: The CEO of Arini Capital Management’s US business Gavin Yates has left the firm, according to people with knowledge of the situation.

title: Billionaire Gilinski, GeoPark Said to be Near Venezuela Oil Deal
summary: Colombia’s richest family is nearing a Venezuela oil deal in conjunction with GeoPark Ltd, a Bogota-based oil company in which it is the largest shareholder with a 28% stake, according to people familiar with the matter who asked for anonymity discussing confidential plans.

title: Tariffs Could Bring Canada Auto "To Its Knees"
summary: President Trump vowed this week to hike tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel to 50% at the start of next year as part of an ongoing trade war threat with the country. Linda Hasenfratz, Executive Chair of Linamar, says that after decades of free trade in automotives between he US and Canada, the implementation of such high tariffs would "cripple the industry." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: What’s Behind the Classic Jackson Hole Photo Op?
summary: For years, the Fed chair would give an address in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and Wall Street and news organizations wouldn't have a recent photo of the chair to accompany stories. In steps Bloomberg's own Mike McKee. Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal and Tom Keene learn the origin of the now traditional "Fed perp walk." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yen Passes 160 Per Dollar to Hit Weakest Level in a Month
summary: The yen moved past 160 per US dollar to its weakest level in a month, extending a slide that’s erased more than half of its intervention-fueled gains.

title: Por qué EE.UU. está detrás de una parte del petróleo de Venezuela
summary: Aunque Venezuela ya no es la gran potencia petrolera que fue en el pasado, el país cuenta con algunas de las mayores reservas de petróleo del mundo. title: Ecuador Court Convicts Former President Moreno of Taking Bribes
summary: Three judges in Ecuador found former President Lenín Moreno guilty of accepting bribes from China’s Sinohydro Corp. Ltd. when he was vice president in 2010, according to a unanimous verdict.

title: Threat of a Fed Rate Hike Is Changing the Leadership in Markets, Slimmon Says
summary: Andrew Slimmon, managing director and head of applied equity advisors at Morgan Stanley, says he's happy with what Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said during his speech at Jackson Hole and he remains consistent. Slimmon says the threat of an interest rate hike is causing a change in leadership in stock markets. He shares more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Funds Add Bullish Gasoline Bets at Fastest Pace in Six Months
summary: Hedge funds boosted their bullish wagers on US gasoline by the most since the US-Iran war began, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data showed.

title: Mexico Sells Samurai Bond for First Time in Two Years
summary: Mexico returned to the Samurai bond market for the first time in two years on Friday, raising ¥282.8 billion ($1.77 billion) amid a rush of issuance as borrowers seek to lock in funding before Japanese interest rates potentially climb further.

title: US Stocks Close Lower After Warsh Speech | Closing Bell
summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Lisa Mateo and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Two-Year Yield Jumps on Warsh’s Inflation Pledge: Markets Wrap
summary: Wall Street traders sent short-term yields sharply higher as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to bring inflation to the target, boosting bets on a rate hike and stabilizing longer-dated bonds.

title: Americans Feel Guilty About Spending Money on Fun
summary: Bloomberg's  Zijia Song joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Almost three-quarters of US adults feel guilty when they spend on things that bring them joy instead of putting the money toward their financial goals. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warsh Is Driving the Bond Market, Whether He Wants to or Not
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has signaled that he wants bond investors to react to underlying changes in the US economy rather than commentary from the central bank. So far, they’re doing the opposite.

title: People Without Kids Now Utilize 529 Accounts
summary: Bloomberg's Sarah Foster joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." In 2022 Congress tweaked the rules covering 529 plans. Now, people without kids are now able to pour money into those accounts after hitting the annual limits for contributing to their retirement plans — treating the 529 as a backdoor for funding a Roth IRA. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Employers Abandon Group Insurance as Price Hikes Bite
summary: Bloomberg's Taylor Nicole Rogers joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." As US employers brace for the largest price hikes on employee health plans in 15 years, a growing number are opting out of group insurance altogether. Instead of providing medical benefits directly, more than 20,000 companies entered Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA) in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: 47% Saw Real Wages Decline Due To Inflation: Richardson
summary: Nela Richardson, chief economist & ESG officer with ADP and Bloomberg contributor, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how all parts of the economy are getting more expensive and how Americans are handling rising prices.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: European Stocks Set for Fifth Monthly Gains in a Row
summary: European stocks gained on Friday and were set for a fifth straight monthly advance, even as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to tackle sticky inflation.

title: Christina Ruffini's Boot Budget
summary: Bloomberg's Christina Ruffini joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss Christina's spendings habits that often center around Frye boots.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Bets, Personal Finance Is Broken: Must-Read Books
summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu, Sarah Foster, and Zijia Song discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money."  (Source: Bloomberg)
